Ophthalmology · published research

Presbyopia

A one-month double-masked randomized trial reported lower asthenopic symptoms and better accommodative amplitude and vision-related quality of life than sham treatment. Longer-term effects remain unknown.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A one-month double-masked randomized trial reported lower asthenopic symptoms and better accommodative amplitude and vision-related quality of life than sham treatment. Longer-term effects remain unknown.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact presbyopia category contains one human publication: a double-masked randomized trial of repeated low-level red-light therapy. It randomized 66 adults, of whom 64 completed the study. No independent replication, animal study, or laboratory study is listed. Song et al. 2026

Human and clinical evidence

The trial evaluated asthenopic symptoms and accommodation in adults with presbyopia over one month. The publication reports significantly reduced asthenopic symptoms, improved accommodative amplitude, and better vision-related quality of life compared with sham treatment. No treatment-related adverse effect was reported during this short study. The number of participants is modest, and the record provides no evidence that the changes persist after treatment stops or improve long-term reading function, spectacle dependence, or daily activities.

Animal evidence

No presbyopia-specific animal treatment study was identified in the mapped category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No in-vitro or ex-vivo presbyopia study was listed.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The trial used repeated 650 nm red light for 180 seconds twice daily over one month. These parameters describe the studied device and population. The result should not be generalized to different devices, exposure schedules, or adults with other eye conditions without further testing.

Interpretation

This trial provides an early controlled signal for short-term symptoms and accommodation, not evidence of lasting correction of presbyopia. Replication with a larger sample and longer follow-up is needed to establish clinical importance, durability, and safety over repeated use.

Evidence strength in source summaryAsthenopic symptoms and accommodation: One short randomized signal Long-term function: Uncertain
Publications and records1 publication: 1 double-masked randomized human trial with 66 randomized participants and 64 completers.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One double-masked randomized trial enrolled 66 adults, with 64 completing one month of treatment. It reported improvement in asthenopic symptoms, accommodative amplitude, and vision-related quality of life without observed adverse effects. The short follow-up and single study do not establish durable benefit.

Publication and study types

  • It is the only clinical cohort in the mapped category.
  • No animal, in-vitro, or ex-vivo publication and no independent replication are listed.
